name: ElementsBoost – Elementor Page Speed & Performance Optimizer
author: Mubashir Taqi

sections.description:
ElementsBoost is a WordPress performance plugin built specifically to help speed up Elementor websites.

Elementor pages can load CSS, JavaScript, fonts, icons, animations, sliders, and addon assets that are not needed everywhere. ElementsBoost helps you find that extra weight and apply practical improvements without editing code.

Version 2.0 introduces a major BuraqOptimizer experience focused on visible results. Buraq scans the current public page, explains what it found inside the Elementor editor, highlights matching elements with X-Ray, and verifies supported actions against fresh page output before showing them as completed.

Meet BuraqOptimizer

BuraqOptimizer is your Elementor performance assistant inside the editor.

  • Scan the public version of the page you are editing
  • Review page-specific performance, content, image, and structure findings
  • See critical, warning, polish, and working states in one panel
  • Use X-Ray to locate matching Elementor elements visually
  • Apply supported one-click actions and rescan for confirmation
  • Review theoretical potential separately from verified results
  • Edit or undo supported content actions such as meta descriptions
  • See an Elementor Optimization Score that complements Google PageSpeed Insights

Buraq does not mark a supported action successful just because a switch was enabled. When a rendered result can be checked, it rescans the public page and reports what it can confirm.

Works with your existing cache plugin

ElementsBoost does not replace a full-page cache or CDN. It complements cache plugins by reducing selected Elementor and WordPress frontend work before the result is cached.

Free Features

  • BuraqOptimizer inside the Elementor editor
  • Public-page scanning with fresh verification for supported actions
  • X-Ray element highlighting with explicit Show and Hide controls
  • Elementor Optimization Score and page findings
  • 14 controls for Elementor assets, icons, animations, sliders, emoji, oEmbed, jQuery Migrate, Gutenberg CSS, Dashicons, fonts, and more
  • Risk labels and potential-impact guidance
  • Smart Onboarding with recommended starting settings
  • PageDNA content and asset scanner
  • Plugin Profiler, Asset Usage Map, Compatibility Warning Engine, and Conflict Guard
  • Settings History with up to 30 snapshots
  • Auto-Revert safety monitoring for supported setting changes
  • Missing image-dimension support for eligible Media Library images
  • Reversible heading, empty-container, YouTube lazy-load, and meta-description actions
  • Reviewable alt-text drafts and undo for eligible Media Library images
  • Optional, administrator-enabled local Real User Monitoring for LCP, CLS, and INP

Go Further with ElementsBoost Pro

Free includes BuraqOptimizer, global controls, profiling, and practical page fixes. Pro adds deeper per-page optimization and before-and-after testing.

Explore ElementsBoost Pro

  • Elementor Lean Mode: remove unused libraries on selected pages instead of relying only on global controls.
  • Safe Preview: privately inspect optimized output before visitors see it.
  • Live PageSpeed Benchmark: run and compare Google PageSpeed tests from WordPress.
  • Critical CSS: create mobile and desktop critical CSS for above-the-fold rendering.
  • JavaScript delay and defer: control non-critical scripts with dependency-aware options.
  • Local image optimization: compress Media Library images, create verified WebP/AVIF files, run bulk jobs, and restore backed-up image families.
  • Third-party addon analysis: detect assets from popular Elementor addon packs.
  • Advanced per-page rules: build more precise optimization rules for complex websites.

See ElementsBoost Pro features and pricing

External Services

Google Fonts

When Self-host Google Fonts is enabled, ElementsBoost downloads CSS and font files from fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com, stores them locally, and serves the local files later.

  • Terms: https://developers.google.com/fonts/terms
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Optional ElementsBoost Diagnostics

When an administrator enables Diagnostics, the plugin sends anonymous technical data weekly to https://elementsboost.com/wp-json/elementsboost-telemetry/v1/collect. This can include WordPress, Elementor and PHP versions, theme name, plugin and Elementor-page counts, enabled controls, and a non-reversible hashed site identifier. It does not include personal data, page URLs, or page content. Diagnostics is off by default.

  • Privacy: https://elementsboost.com/privacy-policy/
  • Terms: https://elementsboost.com/terms-of-service/

ElementsBoost Benchmarks

The dashboard can retrieve aggregated benchmarks from https://elementsboost.com/wp-json/elementsboost-telemetry/v1/benchmarks. The request sends no site or user data and is cached for six hours.

Compatibility Intelligence Feed

When compatibility alerts are enabled, the plugin downloads a curated feed daily from https://elementsboost.com/wp-json/elementsboost-intel/v1/intelligence-feed. It sends no site or user data, is cached for 24 hours, and can be disabled.

Google PageSpeed Insights (Pro)

When a Pro user runs PageSpeed Benchmark, the tested page URL is sent to Google PageSpeed Insights. Results are stored locally for comparison.

  • Terms: https://developers.google.com/terms
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install ElementsBoost from Plugins → Add New in WordPress.
  2. Activate ElementsBoost. Elementor must also be active.
  3. Open ElementsBoost in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Follow Smart Onboarding to review recommended starting settings.
  5. Open a page with Elementor and click the BuraqOptimizer button.
  6. Scan, review the findings, apply the changes you want, and visually check the page.
sections.faq:
Will ElementsBoost automatically make every Elementor website faster?

ElementsBoost can reduce selected frontend assets and resolve supported page findings, but results depend on the theme, hosting, design, plugins, images, cache configuration, and which assets the page genuinely needs. Use Buraq, visual review, and PageSpeed testing together.

What does “verified” mean in BuraqOptimizer?

For actions with a measurable rendered result, Buraq fetches a fresh public-page render and checks for the expected change. If it cannot confirm the result, it keeps the action in a review or unverified state instead of awarding it as completed.

Can I undo Buraq actions?

Supported content actions create a scoped undo record. Buraq checks that the value has not been changed later before restoring it, helping protect newer manual edits. Settings History is available for optimization settings.

Does the image width and height fix cover every image?

It covers eligible rendered image tags when WordPress can resolve local Media Library dimensions. External images, CSS backgrounds, iframes, embeds, and images injected later by JavaScript may require manual work.
sections.changelog:
2.0.0

Our biggest ElementsBoost update yet, built around BuraqOptimizer, visible evidence, safer actions, and a clearer Elementor performance workflow.

  • Buraq now scans the current public page and refreshes its findings when Elementor opens or saves.
  • Supported actions confirm their rendered result before appearing completed.
  • X-Ray now has reliable Show and Hide controls and avoids highlighting already-resolved images.
  • Image conversion reporting separates real delivery confirmation from theoretical potential.
  • Eligible Elementor and widget images receive more reliable width and height support.
  • Meta descriptions, alt-text batches, image batches, and supported content actions have safer scoped undo.
  • Savings reporting clearly separates verified reductions from estimates.
  • Auto-Revert, RUM, XML-RPC controls, and administrator output received a major reliability and security update.
  • Elementor recommendations are more context-aware, reducing common image, font, video, and template false positives.
  • Dashboard findings, action messages, and the Pro upgrade path are easier to understand.

Older release history is available in changelog.txt.
